nodes.name: Direct Phosphorization
nodes.procedure: NiP nanosheet array electrode was prepared from the commercial Ni foam (NF) through a direct phosphorization strategy. Prior to phosphorization, the NF was sonicated for 30 min in 1.0 M HCl solution, acetone and ethanol, respectively. Next, 0.14 g NF (ca. 1×4 cm²) and 1.0 g red phosphorous powder were piled into the porcelain boat individually, where red phosphorous powder was closer to the upstream side. The precursors were reacted in Ar atmosphere for 1 h at 500°C with a heating rate of 5°C min⁻¹. The NiP nanosheet array electrode was obtained after the tube furnace falling to room temperature.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiP Nanosheet Array Electrode: NiP nanosheet array electrode was prepared from the commercial Ni foam (NF) through a direct phosphorization strategy.

nodes.name: Cation Exchange
nodes.procedure: Ni_xCo_{1-x}P nanosheet array electrodes were synthesized by a facile cation-exchange method between NiP nanoarray electrode and Co²⁺ ions. Typically, 49.8 mg cobaltous acetate tetrahydrate was dissolved in 40 mL ethylene glycol. Then, a piece of NiP nanosheet array electrode was immersed into the above mixture solution in a 100 mL autoclave, and then reacted for 12 h at 200 °C. The product was rinsed with water and ethanol three times and desiccated naturally to eventually obtain Ni_{0.96}Co_{0.04}P nanosheet array electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiP shows uniform vertically aligned nanosheet morphology with smooth surface. Ni_{0.96}Co_{0.04}P shows similar nanosheet array with burr-like skin and grain boundaries.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Figure 1d; Figure S1, Supporting Information) of Ni_{0.96}Co_{0.04}P clearly shows a uniform vertically aligned nanosheet morphology analogous to NiP, indicating that Ni_{0.96}Co_{0.04}P inherits nanosheet array morphology characteristic very well after cation exchange.
